question_text: Describe in your own words one painting from this chapter which suggests that the British were more powerful than Indians. How does the artist depict this?
answer_text: The painting which depicts the discovery of the body of Tipu Sultan shows the British as more powerful than Indians. In this painting, the British General is shown as if standing on a high pedestal and exuding all the confidence. On the other hand, Tipu Sultan is shown half naked and lifeless; lying in the dark recess. The painting appears to announce that those who dare to challenge the British authority would meet the same fate.
final_answer: Thus, the painting conveys the message of British supremacy over Indians.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires interpretation and analysis of a painting.

question_text: Why did the scroll painters and potters come to Kalighat? Why did they begin to paint new themes?
answer_text: The scroll painters and potters came to Kalighat in the hope of new patrons and buyers of their art. After the 1 &lOs, a new trend was visible within the Kalighat artists. Living in a society where values, tastes, social norms and customs were undergoing rapid changes, Kalighat artists responded to the world around them and produced paintings on social and political themes.
final_answer: Therefore, they adapted to the changing society by painting new themes.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of social changes and artistic response.

subject: history
chapter_name: the changing world of visual arts
question_text: Why can we think of Raja Ravi Varma's paintings as national?
answer_text: Raja Ravi Varma was one of the first artists who tried to create a style that was both modern and national. He used the Western art of oil painting and realistic life study to paint themes from Indian mythology. He dramatised on canvas scene after scene from the Indian epics Ramayana and Mahabharata. This portrayal of an Indian consciousness is what makes his paintings national. This was perhaps one of the reasons why his paintings were popular not only among Indian princes and art collectors but also among the masses.
final_answer: Thus, his work represents a blend of modernity and Indian tradition.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of cultural significance in art.

subject: history
chapter_name: the changing world of visual arts
question_text: Why did some artists produce cheap popular prints? What influence would such prints have had on the minds of people who looked at them?
answer_text: By the late nineteenth century, mechanical printing presses were set up in different parts of India. This allowed prints to be produced in large numbers. These prints could therefore be sold cheap in the market. As a result, even the poor could buy them. With the spread of nationalism, the popular prints of the early twentieth century began carrying nationalist messages. Such popular prints would have inspired people to fight British rule.
final_answer: Thus, cheap popular prints played a significant role in inspiring people against British rule.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of historical context and the impact of art on society.
